Overall, I love Monarch Money! It does an excellent job of connecting to almost all my financial accounts and has become an invaluable tool for understanding and managing my household finances.

One of its greatest strengths is the ability to track spending across multiple accounts in one place. Instead of reviewing individual bank accounts and credit card statements, I can see where our money is going, identify spending patterns, compare expenses from month to month, and distinguish recurring expenses from occasional purchases. This makes it much easier to understand our actual cost of living, identify opportunities to save, and make informed financial decisions. I particularly appreciate being able to examine individual transactions rather than relying solely on broad spending categories.

I also love the ability to download transactions as CSV files. This allows me to conduct more detailed analysis in Excel, create customized reports, and track spending over longer periods. An option to automate or schedule these exports would make an already excellent feature even better.

The new email receipt system is a fantastic improvement, especially for tracking Apple purchases and subscriptions. Being able to connect receipts to transactions makes it much easier to understand charges that otherwise appear with vague merchant descriptions.

There are, however, a few areas that could be improved.

Account connectivity: Reauthorizing accounts that require two-factor authentication can be frustrating. I wish there were an easier, centralized process for identifying disconnected accounts and reconnecting them.

Duplicate accounts: When a retirement account becomes disconnected and is subsequently reconnected, it can be difficult to determine whether Monarch has created a duplicate. This raises concerns about the accuracy of account balances and net worth calculations. Better duplicate detection and a straightforward way to reconcile accounts without losing transaction history would be extremely helpful.

Transfers versus income: Monarch could do a better job distinguishing actual income and expenses from transfers between accounts. Internal transfers, credit card payments, and certain retirement transactions can distort income and spending reports when they are incorrectly categorized. Better automatic identification and reconciliation would significantly improve the reliability of its financial reporting.

Despite these issues, Monarch is an excellent product. It has given me a much clearer picture of our household finances and made tracking spending considerably easier. I especially appreciate that it provides both an accessible overview of our finances and the flexibility to conduct more detailed analysis when I want to dig deeper.

I've been so picky over the years and tried so many different services, but I always ended up back in a spreadsheets. Infinite configurability, but more manual. That said, I found a middle ground about six months ago. The spreadsheet tracks the budget, brokerage contributions, statistics, and savings (think monthly money being set aside for yearly payments and such), and then I use Monarch Money for tracking transactions. Manually tracking my transactions in the spreadsheet was just so tedious and having Monarch handle that via Plaid and the three-ish other services that fill the same space has been nice. One issue I have that isn't the fault of any app or service is that there are still plenty of banks that don't support OAuth for reading data. The big ones I use all support it no problem, but my primary, smaller (not tiny) bank and even Discover want you to use your _same_ username and password along with a checkbox in the settings to "allow third party access". They don't tell you what is limited via that third party access either, so I can't tell if it allows read-only when there's no MFA involved or what. In those cases, I still manually input transactions, but it's the vast minority of my transactions. Monarch will give you notifications for transactions, overages on budgets, etc, but I bet any half decent service will do the same at this point.
